tagline: Bloomfield preserves the military newspaper that Union soldiers began in 1861
intro: Missouri Route 25 reaches Bloomfield 6.5 miles north of Dexter. Bloomfield is the Stoddard County seat, with Civil War sites identified by markers.

In November 1861, Colonel Richard J. Oglesby brought Union troops to Bloomfield under General Ulysses S. Grant’s orders to capture M. Jeff Thompson. Confederate forces had abandoned the town. Ten soldiers who were printers requested its local press; Oglesby approved, and they produced the first Stars and Stripes.

Approaching from Dexter, follow Route 25 north to Bloomfield. The Stars and Stripes National Museum and Library is at 17377 Stars and Stripes Way. The town’s courthouse has a large clock tower above its roof.

moments.title: Stars and Stripes National Museum and Library
moments.text: The newspaper’s first print edition is preserved in Bloomfield, where soldiers began publishing it during the Civil War. That first venture produced four editions before publication stopped until World War I. In 1918, General John J. Pershing authorized its revival for the American Expeditionary Forces in France. The museum now documents that publishing history through more than 10,000 square feet of multimedia exhibits and a collection of over 20,000 artifacts. Its public archives include newspaper editions spanning over 160 years. Free library services and research support extend the museum’s work beyond its exhibits.

moments.title: Stoddard County Courthouse
moments.text: Bloomfield’s courthouse took shape in two stages. Built between 1867 and 1870, it began as a two-story brick building on a concrete foundation. An enlargement and remodeling in 1909 gave it its Classical Revival treatment. Above the hipped cross-gable roof rises a large clock tower. The courthouse entered the National Register of Historic Places in 1984.
moments.notice: Look for the clock tower above the courthouse’s hipped cross-gable roof.

moments.title: Bloomfield
moments.text: Bloomfield was platted in 1835 and took its name from wildflowers in the vicinity. Its Civil War history has a visible presence in markers identifying sites in the area. Soldiers of the 11th, 18th and 29th Illinois Regiments camped here on November 9, 1861; the first Stars and Stripes was printed during that occupation.
